image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Begin reducing visible plug tilt while compensating around its tip; retain grasp and keep clearance above socket.
Continue leveling the connector and shift its image center toward the slot; preserve an approach gap.
Horizontal centering improved. Continue the pitch correction about the plug tip and approach slowly from above.
Bring hand close to level while keeping the connector centered over the socket, descending about two millimeters.
Plug remains retained and visually centered; approach vertically in a small increment while watching the remaining gap.
Advance gently toward the slot with the current alignment; the image still shows a small clearance.
Close the last visible gap using submillimeter downward steps, retaining the connector and watching for seating.
The connector is at the slot mouth. Apply only a short, slow insertion increment; seating depth remains uncertain from this view.
The plug tip is no longer advancing with the hand. Relieve contact, then make a small depth-alignment correction toward the camera before retrying.
The connector did not clearly follow the last lift. Narrow the gripper target and make a tiny lift to check retention before further alignment.
Lift a few millimeters with the firmer grip to clear the slot rim and verify that the plug follows; depth alignment is still uncertain.
The lift now visibly retained the plug. Adjust its depth toward the socket center while keeping several millimeters of vertical clearance.
Approach the socket again after the depth correction, maintaining the firmer grasp and level orientation.
Close the small remaining tip-to-slot gap with slow vertical steps; watch whether the connector continues moving with the hand.
The tip has reached the mouth of the slot; make a one-millimeter insertion attempt without changing lateral alignment.
Tip motion appears constrained at the mouth. Relieve contact and try a one-millimeter depth correction rather than pushing farther.
The plug still does not visibly follow short lifts. Close the remaining gripper opening and lift two millimeters to restore controlled clearance.
Increase clearance modestly and allow the closed grasp to settle; verify the plug follows before another seating attempt.
The plug now visibly follows the lift. Try a smaller depth offset away from the camera while lowering only within the visible clearance.
Continue straight down by 1.5 mm at this revised depth alignment, watching the tip against the socket rim.
The plug followed the last descent to the socket mouth. Continue another short insertion increment while preserving alignment.
The tip stopped advancing. Lift to unload it, then test a 1.5 mm correction away from the camera and a very small lateral recentering.
Allow the grasp and contact to settle, then probe downward slowly at the revised depth without accumulating a large push.
Maintain the revised alignment and advance gently another millimeter; the black housing may obscure the inserted tip.
Continue a limited slow seating motion at the same alignment, keeping the gripper closed and monitoring the housing.
Repeated straight probes are constrained. Unload the rim and test a small pitch correction about the connector tip before reseating.
Lower slowly at the revised pitch, checking whether the connector enters rather than stopping on the rim.
The tip remains rim-constrained. Unload slightly and correct the small apparent cross-slot tilt, compensating translation to keep the tip centered.
Hold the closed grasp briefly so the connector can settle after the small angular correction; inspect its position before another probe.
Create clear vertical separation for a larger depth re-alignment; the current rim contact has not produced visible insertion.
With the plug visibly lifted, shift away from the camera to test the socket depth suggested by the block's top-plane perspective.
Descend through the visible clearance at the farther depth position, stopping near the socket mouth for inspection.
The plug is still above the slot. Reduce the final clearance with a controlled 2.5 mm descent at the revised depth.
The farther-depth trial is blocked above the slot image. Lift fully clear before revising plug pitch rather than pushing on the rim.
With clear separation, revise pitch toward the original grasp attitude and remove the added cross-slot tilt, approximately pivoting around the tip while shifting it slightly nearer the camera.
Approach again with the revised pitch, lowering through the visible gap and retaining the plug.
Close the remaining visible gap at the revised pitch, monitoring the top of the connector as well as its occluded tip.
The tip is still stopping above the socket. Lift clear to correct the connector's visible angular offset rather than repeat the same insertion.
With the tip clear, correct the visible twist of the plug in small yaw increments, approximately keeping its tip above the socket.
Level the plug's slightly sloped lower edge while maintaining clearance and shift its depth modestly toward the socket center.
Descend through most of the visible clearance with the revised angular alignment, stopping short of a large insertion push.
The tip is at the slot mouth and its edge is more level. Recenter slightly left, then attempt a short slow insertion.
Tip motion is constrained at the mouth. Test a small nearer-camera depth correction with almost no additional downward motion.
Further level the plug's lower edge with a small compensated roll adjustment, relieving contact slightly instead of forcing insertion.
Lift clear of the rim to let the angular adjustment transfer to the connector and obtain an unobstructed alignment check.
With the plug clear and its lower edge now more level, reduce the remaining visible side-face twist using a compensated yaw adjustment.
The plug appears less twisted and stays retained; descend through half the visible gap before checking the slot alignment again.
Approach another three millimeters and recenter the tip slightly right over the socket before contact.
Close the last small gap slowly at the revised alignment, watching for continued connector motion into the slot.
The housing is at the socket mouth; continue a limited two-millimeter seating motion without lateral or angular changes.
The housing remains stopped at the rim. Lift fully clear to assess the plug's own orientation rather than continue downward against contact.
The free plug's lower edge is now level. Test a modest pitch change about its tip, preserving the visible socket clearance and lateral centering.
Approach vertically at the revised pitch, leaving a small visible gap for the final alignment check.
Close the remaining visible clearance with a three-millimeter descent, preserving the current plug alignment.
Perform a shallow depth-alignment sweep toward the camera at the slot mouth, with only half a millimeter of downward travel and slight lateral recentering.
The tip moved toward the slot during the sweep; attempt a short vertical seating motion at this depth alignment.
Continue a limited slow seating motion at the current alignment; the housing obscures the plug tip, so completion is not yet established.
Relieve contact and shift the plug slightly left to correct its visible offset from the slot center before another seating attempt.
The lower edge is centered laterally but appears just in front of the slot. Make a small away-camera depth correction with a shallow seating motion.
The socket may be hiding the advancing tip. Try a bounded three-millimeter vertical seating motion, checking the housing rather than the occluded lower edge.
